# Churchill Downs Update: Longtime Trainer Charles 'Scooter' Dickey Dies at 85


## Nov 18, 2026


Charles “Scooter” Dickey, a fixture on the Churchill Downs backstretch whose training career spanned nearly six decades, died Saturday at age 85.


Dickey began riding races at age 12 on a half-mile track in his hometown of Anthony, Kan. His father had nicknamed him Scooter for the way he scooted around as a baby. He rode for about 10 years before he could no longer make weight.


“You can call it weight problems but I like to refer to it as ‘feed tub problems,’” Dickey joked in a 2019 Churchill Downs interview.


Dickey won his first race as a trainer in 1963 at Centennial Park in Littleton, Colo. Dickey stabled primarily in the Midwest before he and his wife, Dana, moved their stable to Kentucky in 1992.


“Lots of top trainers got their start in Anthony, which was only home to a couple thousand people,” said fellow trainer Randy Morse, Dickey’s former son-in-law. “I think that’s where he gained most of his horsemanship. He knew how to train one, that’s for sure. He had a lot of really good horses on the Midwest circuit that didn’t gain a whole lot of national notoriety.”


Arguably Dickey’s best horse was Preston Stables’ Flat Out, who overcame a shoulder injury and recurring foot problems before winning the 2011 Suburban Handicap (GII) at Belmont Park. Flat Out returned to Belmont to give Dickey his first Grade I victory in the $750,000 Jockey Club Gold Cup when he beat Drosselmeyer by 2 ¼ lengths. Flat Out was Dickey’s only Breeders’ Cup starter and fifth as the 7-2 favorite in the 2011 Classic (GI) at Churchill Downs.


On or off the racetrack, Dickey loved telling jokes and could reel them off from memory. He played practical jokes during morning training and his friends on the backstretch gave it right back to him.


“He was scared to death of snakes,” Churchill Downs clocker John Nichols said. “I remember one time I bought one of those rubber snakes and I’d have people play jokes on him around the backside. That same snake got passed around to different people to play jokes on him. One morning, the outrider hid it in his vest. Scooter was standing on the outside fence with Rick Hiles and a bunch of those guys. He threw the snake and I saw Scooter jump and scatter. He called me up a few minutes later and told me to look over in my binoculars. He had his pocket knife out and was cutting the snake up into a hundred pieces and that pile of snake sat on the outside rail the rest of the meet.”


Dickey retired in 2019, his 57th year as a trainer. Since 1970, Equibase credits him with 837 wins, 855 seconds, 902 thirds and $13,990,424 in purse earnings from 7,647 starts. He sent out his last starter Dec. 1 that year at Churchill Downs.


Instead of a formal funeral service, his family asked for friends and colleagues to share their memories here: www.facebook.com/share/p/1AKxZPVv1N.


PENULTIMATE WEEK OF FALL MEET FEATURES $300,000 COMMONWEALTH TURF – Saturday’s $300,000 Commonwealth Turf (Grade III) leads the penultimate week of racing of the Fall Meet.


WEDNESDAY, NOV. 18 – PAGODE FACES FAMILIAR RIVALS; SENIOR DAY
Carl R. Moore Management’s Pagode takes off blinkers and faces familiar rivals in Wednesday’s featured $127,000 allowance at 1 1/8 miles in Race 8 at 4:25 p.m. Trained by Joe Sharp, Pagode is the 7-2 morning-line favorite with Luis Saez aboard. The Constitution gelding finished fourth behind Freddie B, C McGriff and Rugged Love in an Oct. 21 allowance at Keeneland. C McGriff and Rugged Love also return Wednesday, while Cherie DeVaux-trained Commentate makes his first start against winners following a neck victory Oct. 3 at Keeneland. Axel Concepcion has the mount on Commentate.
Wednesday also is Senior Day. Guests 60 and older can enjoy lunch and a day at the races on Millionaires Row for $50. Reservations are available by calling (502) 636-4450.
THURSDAY, NOV. 19 – NYCON LEADS ALLOWANCE; $1.6 MILLION DAYTON DEBUTS
Icon Racing Stable’s Nycon is the 5-2 morning-line favorite in Thursday’s featured $127,000 allowance for fillies and mares at 1 1/8 miles in Race 8 at 4:25 p.m. Whit Beckman trains the 3-year-old Nyquist filly, who finished sixth in the Alabama (GI) before running third in an Oct. 1 allowance at Belmont Park. Saez has the mount. Her rivals include C R K Stable’s last-out maiden winner She’s Our Girl, trained by Peter Eurton and ridden by Brian Hernandez Jr., and Walmac Farm’s Leinani, who finished third at Keeneland last month for trainer Chad Brown. Tyler Gaffalione has the call on Leinani.
Earlier in the card, Windancer Farm’s Dayton, a $1.6 million Keeneland September Yearling Sale purchase, makes his debut in a $120,000 maiden special weight for 2-year-olds at one mile in Race 7 at 3:55 p.m. Florent Geroux rides the Not This Time colt for Brad Cox, who also entered Spendthrift Farm’s Capitola, third on debut at Keeneland, with Saez aboard.
FRIDAY, NOV. 20 – PLENSA RETURNS TO ALLOWANCE COMPANY; EAGLES FLIGHT BACK IN ACTION
Mill Ridge Farm and Frank Garrison’s multiple stakes winner Plensa returns to allowance company in Friday’s featured $141,000 allowance optional claimer at 1 1/16 miles on turf in Race 9 at 4:55 p.m. The Rusty Arnold II trainee won the Tapit Stakes at Kentucky Downs before finishing seventh in the Turf Mile (GI) at Keeneland. Geroux has the mount.
One race earlier, Hronis Racing and Summer Wind Equine’s Eagles Flight makes his first start in 17 months in a $134,000 allowance optional claimer at 6 ½ furlongs. The 5-year-old Curlin horse, a half-brother to unbeaten 2022 Horse of the Year Flightline, makes his first start for DeVaux with Jose Ortiz aboard.
SATURDAY, NOV. 21 – REMEMBER MAMBA RETURNS FOR COMMONWEALTH TURF
C R K Stable’s American Turf (GI) runner-up Remember Mamba returns to Churchill Downs to face eight rivals in Saturday’s 21st running of the $300,000 Commonwealth Turf (GIII). The 1 1/16-mile race for 3-year-olds goes as Race 10 at 5:25 p.m. Trained by DeVaux, Remember Mamba won the Transylvania (GIII) at Keeneland in April before finishing second in the American Turf on Kentucky Derby Day. He subsequently finished third in the Belmont Derby (GI), fourth in the Saratoga Derby (GI) and third in the Bryan Station (GII). Jose Ortiz rides from post 8.
SUNDAY, NOV. 22 – TWO $134,000 TURF ALLOWANCES; STAKES ROOM BRUNCH
Amerman Racing Stables’ Zakinthos returns to turf following an 8 ¼-length victory in an off-the-turf allowance at Keeneland in Sunday’s $134,000 allowance optional claimer at 5 ½ furlongs. Saez retains the mount for Brian Lynch in Race 3 at 1:58 p.m.
In Race 7 at 3:55 p.m., a wide-open field of 11 turf specialists are set for a $134,000 allowance optional claimer at 1 1/8 miles on turf in Race 7 at 3:55 p.m.
Sunday’s Stakes Room Brunch begins at noon. Packages are $90 for adults and $45 for children and include seating and access to the brunch buffet.
MEET LEADERS – SAEZ, COX, GODOLPHIN TOP STANDINGS THROUGH 14 DAYS
Through 14 days of the Fall Meet, Saez led the standings 23 victories, an 11-win advantage over Gaffalione and Yomar Ortiz Jr., who are tied for second with 12 apiece. Jaime Torres follows with 10 victories and Jose Ortiz has nine.
Cox led the trainer standings with 13 wins from 31 starters, a 42% strike rate. Steve Asmussen is second with 11 wins, followed by Sharp with nine and Eddie Kenneally with five.
Godolphin topped the owner standings with six victories, followed by Asmussen with four and Epic Horses with three.
WAGERING HIGHLIGHTS THROUGH 14 DAYS
Through the first 14 days of Churchill Downs’ Fall Meet, the average $2 win payoff was $13.52 and the average $2 exacta returned $94.11. The $3 late Pick 3 averaged an $1,800 payoff with pools averaging $161,757, while the 50-cent Pick 5 averaged $7,163 with an average pool of $232,169. The 20-cent Derby City 6 averaged a $28,566 payoff with daily pools averaging $85,898.
LOOKING AHEAD TO THANKSGIVING WEEK
Ten stakes are scheduled from Thanksgiving Day through closing day, including the $700,000 Clark presented by Norton Healthcare (GII) on Friday, Nov. 27. The Clark is expected to feature Wathnan Racing’s Travers Stakes (GI) winner Leading Change along with recent Breeder’s Cup Dirt Mile (GI) runners Bracket Buster and Chunk of Gold.
The Road to the Kentucky Derby and Road to the Kentucky Oaks return Saturday, Nov. 28, with the $400,000 Kentucky Jockey Club (GII) and $400,000 Fasig-Tipton Golden Rod (GII) on the Stars of Tomorrow II program.
Kentucky Derby Future Wager Pool 2 and the Kentucky Derby Sire Future Wager are scheduled for Nov. 26-29. First post on Thanksgiving Day is 11:30 a.m.
DOWN THE STRETCH
Churchill Downs unveiled the official 2027 Kentucky Derby and Kentucky Oaks artwork Tuesday by Lexington, Ky. artist Kayla Weber Nord. Nord will sign prints Friday, Nov. 27, from 2-4 p.m. in the Churchill Downs Store inside the Paddock Gate. For more information, visit www.churchilldowns.com.
